prediction: DOES #44's SKEW BOUND CLOSE THE DESKTOP INSTABILITY THIS LANE MEASURED? The orchestrator reports #79 diagnosed as #44's guest<->pgraph skew on VERTEX DATA, closed on device by HAKUX_FIFO_SKEW_BOUND 0 vs 1 (7 wrong of 64 observations -> 0 of 64), and says this lane's Surface_pitch::Swizzle finding is the same family. It is testable here without a device and without a code change: the bound lives in pfifo.c, is renderer-agnostic, and is read from the environment at runtime. WHAT THIS LANE ALREADY MEASURED, and it is the prior rather than a new guess: Surface_pitch::Swizzle is the only capture of 236 that varies run to run on the desktop GL lane; three runs of one unchanged binary on the full disc scored 14,848 every time with up to 2,341 px differing between them; and the mechanism was traced to the guest overwriting one shared texture buffer at 0272b000 under a queued draw, because Pushbuffer::End() does not wait for the GPU and pgraph reads texture memory when it REACHES the draw. docs/investigations/gl-surface-to-texture-is-wrong.md already names the remedy as widening the CPU-write stall, and pfifo.c's own comment describes the bound as 'hold the guest at its own submission point until PGRAPH has caught up'. That is the same remedy, already built by another lane. PREDICTED: (1) with the bound at 0, Surface_pitch::Swizzle gives MORE THAN ONE distinct capture over three runs; (2) with the bound at 1, it gives EXACTLY ONE over three runs; (3) Pixel_shader::Passthru, the other test on the disc, is byte-stable in BOTH arms -- the control that says the bound is not simply changing everything. NOT PREDICTED: the score. The bound may also move the capture toward the golden, since the race is what loses the inner quad colours, but this lane has no registered value for that and will report it as an observation. WHAT WOULD REFUTE ME: the capture still varying at bound=1, which would say the Swizzle instability is NOT the skew and the two findings are different families despite the shared shape. A null arm -- one distinct capture in BOTH -- is INCONCLUSIVE rather than a pass, because three runs at bound=0 could miss a defect this lane has only ever seen fire some of the time; in that case the arm must be widened before anything is claimed. METHOD NOTE, and it is unusual: the binary under test is built from the PEER branch 80512e37, which carries the bound and does NOT carry this lane's #66, #71 or #51 fixes. That is deliberate -- the question is whether the bound removes the run-to-run variance WITHIN one tree, which is a valid comparison in any tree. Absolute scores from this arm are not comparable with this lane's other numbers. Clear all four shader caches between arms or nothing regenerates.
